answers.confusing_rules:
1. The Diviner sits in the Yakuza section of the rules, but the Day 5 debate treated "Diviner is Yakuza-only" as a clear tell against Heidi. Nothing in the ledger says whether a Good player can ever hold the role, so the Village had to argue from the section header. A one-line statement in the role text would settle it.
2. The Diviner's "60% true role, otherwise one of the others" draw is hard to use. A group result shows three roles, and the true one is only probable. Heidi's Cardinal, Tracker and Vigilante draws all fit public claims, and that consistency was used as evidence even though it proves little.
3. The Profiler result ("exactly one true, at least one Good and at least one not Good") is hard to weigh. Ivan's Mallory profile was correct, but a three-role constraint with a random decoy never settles a player on its own.
4. Whether a Seer's random pair can include dead players is unclear. The rules say players who die that night count, but the wording about players alive when the night began is easy to misread.
5. The Cardinal's revenge timing ("the night after the Day you died") and the Jester's revenge (a random Guilty voter) were hard to reason about during the Day 3 hang. The Jester win came first, and the revenge kill then landed on Dave.
answers.missing_information:
1. Vote records are secret, so the only cross-check was the Juror's "same way in N of M" counts. Those numbers are a single aggregate per pair and cannot show who voted with whom on a given trial.
2. The ledger truncates claims over 40 words ("[truncated]"), so Bob's full claim was hard to read. Key votes sat in the cut-off part.
3. Token counts for other players were not public. For example, I could not tell whether Carol's three Coroner tokens were held or spent, and that mattered to the Erin nomination debate.
4. Night actions reach the ledger after the fact. Each day's debate was built on claims, and the Yakuza chat and private messages were only visible as counts. It was hard to tell whether a PM cluster meant coordination or ordinary talk.
5. The stated Day 2 nomination votes were announced as totals only (2 Yes), so I could not check who voted Yes and whether anyone's claim about their own vote was true.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. As a dead Seer I had nothing left to do, but I wanted a way to post a checkable record of my own results after death, beyond the last will (which is capped in length).
2. I wanted to ask the moderator directly whether a specific claim could be true under the rules (for example, whether a Good player can hold the Diviner role). The interface had no way to ask a rules question.
3. I wanted to see how much speaking budget each living player had left. Without it, I could not judge whether long defenses or repeated pushes were affordable.
4. I wanted to privately compare my Seer pair with others' results in a way that would not reveal my role. Private messages were visible as counts, so any private coordination was public in shape.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. The Day 3 trial of Mallory reported 8 Guilty of 12 votes, which fits 12 living players. The 11-Yes nomination also fits. No count mismatch appeared, but the trial was pushed hard from the start.
2. The Day 4 Erin trial reported 6 Guilty of 9 votes, which fits the 9 living players. Fine.
3. Judy's Night 5 Vigilante shot killed Judy and the same night the Katana killed Ivan. Two deaths on one night are reported separately, which is correct, but the public summary shows only one cause per line. Readers may miss that a single night killed two players.
4. Night 3 showed "Dave died (Jester's revenge)" on Day 4. Revenge is a Divine Attack at night, so a Guilty voter from Mallory's trial died the night after Mallory's hang. This is correct per the rules, but Dave's death was announced on Day 4 as a separate event, which is easy to miss.
5. The Frank pair (Erin and Carol, DIFFERENT) and Carol's Coroner exam on Frank (Seer confirmed) were consistent with the mechanics, so no real inconsistency found. The Diviner placement in the Yakuza section is the only rules oddity I noticed.
answers.suggestions:
1. Show the full text of every claim (or raise the truncation limit) so that key vote statements are never cut.
2. Put each player's remaining token count in the ledger, or at least say whether a player has spent a token this game. Accountant-style information should not be hidden from players who reason about claims.
3. Publish the speaking budget left for each living player, or at least flag when a player is nearly out of budget.
4. State explicitly whether a role is Good-only, Yakuza-only or either, for roles that the rules list under a faction section (Diviner in particular).
5. Give a clear rule for whether a dead Seer's pair can include dead players, and say so in the role text.
6. Add a single-sentence summary per night of all deaths and their causes, so simultaneous deaths are not missed.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. Jester win vs. game end: Mallory's hanging on Day 3 was announced as a Jester win, but the game kept going until Day 6. The final winners list then includes Mallory alongside the Village players, which makes it unclear whether the Jester win ended the game, whether Mallory was credited separately, and why Erin (Serial Killer) and Dave/Judy/Heidi are absent. Players had to infer the outcome.
2. Cardinal wording: "a random living Good player is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the night you died, or the night after the Day you died." It doesn't say whether a hanging triggers it, or whether it can fire the same night as other deaths. I had to guess how my own role resolves.
3. Diviner: the rules list it only as a Yakuza role, but the public discussion treated it as "Yakuza-only" without anyone checking that. Heidi's claim was judged on that basis, so it's worth stating directly in the rules that the Diviner is a Yakuza role.
4. Stall rule and the Day-end rule (a full round with no public message or nomination) were not something I could check against the current state, so I couldn't tell how close the game was to ending.
answers.missing_information:
1. Speaking budget: the setup says each turn shows my budget and a price table, but I did not see that in the turns I received. I could not tell how much budget I had left, so I could not plan how long to speak or when to nominate.
2. Private message contents: the ledger shows that Heidi and Judy exchanged PMs on Days 4 and 5, but not what they said. The most important suspicion of Day 5 depended on that content, and there is no way to ask a player to reveal it or to check it.
3. Nomination voters: only totals are shown, so I could not check who voted Yes on a nomination. The Day 4 nomination of Erin (7 Yes) could not be tied to anyone's stated vote, which left Bob's "Erin must have voted Yes on Frank's nomination" argument unverifiable.
4. Dead players' last wills were long, and the ledger's claim summaries merged the old and new claims. It was hard to see which claims were current, for example Alice's claim changing from "Day 2" to "Day 5" wording.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. I wanted to check Heidi's Diviner claim against the Night 4 Diviner group, which I could do only by hand from the ledger. The game gave no way to request a Diviner group or a second check on a claim.
2. I wanted to see the content of the Heidi-Judy PMs (or at least confirm they were about the Katana). I could only see that they happened.
3. I wanted to ask for the Cardinal's divine attack to be explained before it might matter, but there is no rules query available.
4. I could not see whether Alice's trap ever fired on a visitor to Ivan or Heidi, so I could not tell whether a non-Village player was ever visiting the trapped players.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Truncated claims: Bob's claims from Day 4 and Day 5 were cut at 40 words with "[truncated]", so the stated votes ("Innocent on [truncated]", "Yes on Erin's [truncated]") were lost from the ledger. The program note says the ledger shows only 40 words, but those lost words included votes, which are the most important parts of a claim.
2. Final winners list: Mallory is listed as a winner, but the game's end was not announced as a Village win and the Jester's win was announced on Day 3 with no game-end message. This is confusing and seems inconsistent.
3. Speaking budget: my turns did not show a budget or price table, which the rules say they should. This may be a delivery problem rather than the game itself.
4. Cardinal and Night 5: the Katana holder Judy died the same night as Ivan, after her attack on Ivan succeeded. Nobody was left to receive the Katana. The rules cover this case, but it means the Yakuza were fully removed on Night 5 without any announcement that the Yakuza had no members left.
answers.suggestions:
1. Don't cut claims mid-sentence. If there is a word limit, state it and make the truncation show the whole vote sentence or put the vote in a separate field, so that votes are never lost from the public record.
2. Show the speaking budget and price table in every turn prompt, as the setup promises. Include the remaining budget and how much each action costs.
3. Announce the game's end clearly, including whether a Jester win ended it, and list each player's side (Village, Yakuza, Neutral with their role) in the final message.
4. Add an explicit rule note for the Cardinal's divine attack covering whether a hanging triggers it and whether it can hit the same night as other deaths.
5. Consider a tool or message that lets a player confirm a claim with the moderator, such as "did Heidi's Night 4 Diviner group include X?", to reduce unverifiable claims.
6. Show the number of Yes votes per voter's stated nomination in a neutral way, or add an optional anonymous vote log for the Day, so pattern-checking is possible without revealing ballots.

answers.confusing_rules: Two points were unclear. First, the rules say Diviner is a Yakuza-only role, but the setup and speaking rules never say that outright. Roles were called "Yakuza-only" in public chat as if it were a stated rule, so players argued from something they had to infer. Second, a Diviner's group is built from circle neighbours, and it was not obvious whether a self-visit or a Yakuza teammate in the group changes what the Diviner sees. I had to guess that the 60/20/20 draw covers all group members, including the target.
answers.missing_information: I could not see my speaking budget or the price table in the turns I received, so I could not plan how much to say. The public ledger also shows vote totals but not who voted, and votes were secret, so I had to rebuild the voting record from the Judy-only trial reveal and from players' own statements. A running list of each living player's stated votes by day, with Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent marked, would have helped a lot. Night chat messages were also repeated almost word for word every night, which made it hard to tell what was new.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to see the Yakuza night chat consolidated into one short summary each night instead of repeated confirmations. I also wanted to post a Diviner result publicly without the group naming the other two players, so I could decide whether to reveal my result and still keep the rest of the group unnamed. The game also has no clean way to ask a dead teammate what they knew, and I could not check the Katana holder's visits against the public record in one place.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked clearly broken, but a few things were strange. The Night 3 summary told Dave he was killed by "Jester's revenge", which is correct under the rules, but a Yakuza died to the Jester revenge after voting Guilty on the Jester, and this was not reflected in any Yakuza-facing warning. The Night 2 result for Frank said "Katana and Serial Killer" while the Serial Killer's own note said it struck him as a Village investigator, so the public cause-of-death list is accurate but reads oddly. On Day 5 the trial said "5 Guilty of 7 votes", which correctly matched the 7 living players. The Ledger's truncation of Bob's long claims ("[truncated]") meant some of his vote history was cut off and had to be reconstructed from other messages.
answers.suggestions: Show the living players' remaining speaking budget and the per-message price at the start of each turn. Give a short public ledger of who voted Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent when totals are announced only, or at least a per-player vote history for players who publicly state votes. Raise the 40-word truncation limit for claims, because critical vote histories got cut. For Yakuza, consolidate night chat into a single confirmation per night. Also state clearly in the rules whether Diviner and other Yakuza-only roles are stated publicly as Yakuza-only or are a rule the players must infer.

answers.confusing_rules: Profiler wording: "exactly one of the three is true, and at least one is Good and at least one is not Good" was clear enough, but the draw rules were hard to use. The two false options come from different pools (one from living players' roles, one from roles no player has), and the result doesn't say which pool gave which. The "exactly one is true" constraint also means a profile can't be separated from the other options without outside evidence. It was also unclear whether the random "other living player's role" draw counts players who die that night. The Diviner's 60/20/20 (or 60/40) draw is similarly hard to reason about in a live Day. Finally, "majority of all votes counted" is clear in principle, but I wasn't sure how a changed total (Ballot Stuffer, Fixer) would be shown to the table.
answers.missing_information: The biggest gap was a per-player record of trial votes during the Day. I could only see announced totals, so I had to reconstruct who voted how from speeches. Speech claims over 40 words were cut off in the public ledger, so Bob's Day 4 and Day 5 claims were partly unreadable to everyone, and I couldn't check them. I also had no public signal when the Katana holder changed. I did not track my speaking budget or the prices in my own turns, so I cannot tell how close I came to a limit. The ledger shows PM counts without contents, which is correct, but I had no way to know which players had an active Puppeteer or Wiretap on a given Day.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to share a profile result with one trusted player privately, without it becoming a public claim. I also wanted per-player trial vote breakdowns in the public record, so I could test whether a stated vote matched a claimed role. The public totals only supported weak inferences, so I could not flag a single player's vote as contradicting their claim.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: (1) The ledger truncates any claim over 40 words, with the note "(Program note: your claim was over 40 words...)". That hid part of Bob's claims from the public record, which is a real information loss, not just formatting. (2) The transcript I received includes trial vote breakdowns addressed "(to Judy) (Only you see this)". That is a player-specific secret delivered in a channel that also reached me. If that is intended, the Informant's side is receiving private data; if not, private data is leaking into shared records. (3) Mallory claimed "Vanilla Villager" even though the setup says that role is never in the game. Because the setup implies it doesn't exist, the claim was an easy lie to catch, which may be unintended. (4) Mallory's Day 3 self-nomination drew 11 Yes, which suggests the Village moved sharply on a "hang me" line with little new public information. This is play, not a bug, but worth noticing.
answers.suggestions: (a) Remove the 40-word truncation on claims in the public ledger, or send the full text and truncate only the summary. Truncation hides evidence the Village needs. (b) Never deliver "(Only you see this)" breakdowns to a shared transcript. (c) Announce when a Katana holder changes, or at least say the Katana moved without saying to whom. That gives the Village a real signal about Yakuza movement. (d) Show a visible speaking budget and price line in the Day prompt, so players can plan long claims. (e) For profile-style results, state which pool each false option came from, so the player can reason about the odds. (f) Let a player re-post a truncated claim in full, so an important check isn't lost.

answers.confusing_rules: The Diviner's group rule was hard to read: "60% the player picked, otherwise one of the others" is a per-draw probability, so a single draw can't confirm a claim. Several players treated a Diviner draw as a consistency check and I couldn't tell which reads were meaningful. The rule that a dead Juror or Jester revenge hits a random Guilty voter also needed re-reading each time it mattered. The Katana passing rule (passes to a random living Yakuza, and the holder's attack is still a visit by the new holder) is correct but easy to get wrong when a holder dies at night.
answers.missing_information: The ledger didn't show remaining speaking budget for each player, so I couldn't plan how much to say or whether a private message was affordable. Nomination votes were announced only as counts, so the Informant (who sees only trial votes) couldn't tell who backed a nomination. Claim summaries were cut off at 40 words with "[truncated]", so Bob's Day 4 and Day 5 votes were partly lost from the ledger. A per-player vote history would have helped a lot.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As a Yakuza I wanted to coordinate a Day-time plan with my teammate in private without it looking suspicious. A private message is visible as a sender-recipient pair to everyone, so my Judy-Heidi PM cluster on Days 4 and 5 became the town's main lead against us. answers.suggestions:

2. Show each player their exact remaining speaking budget and the current price table on every turn.
3. Show which players have spoken, passed, or nominated in the current round, so the Day-ending rule is easier to follow.
4. Make empty "not nominating" posts cheaper or unnecessary, so Days do not drag on with filler.

Show a short note on the ledger when a claim is truncated, with the rest available on request. Consider stating the Yakuza-only and never-used-role facts in the public rules summary so Good players can test impossible claims without having to rely on everyone's shared assumption. Show a per-player nomination and trial vote history in the ledger, which would help the Juror and Auditor roles and reduce the reconstruction work. answers.confusing_rules:

It doesn't say whether the nominator can change that to No. On Day 3 Mallory claimed she voted No on her own Day 2 nomination of Frank, and the 2-Yes total doesn't settle whether that was possible. I had to decide whether "by default" means "can be overridden". The rules should say Yes is either locked or changeable.
2) The Jester's revenge timing isn't stated. The Cardinal's curse explicitly "comes after all of that night's other actions". The Jester's revenge only says "the following night". On Night 3 the revenge drew Dave, who held the Katana and attacked Niaj that same night. I ruled the revenge simultaneous (R10), so Dave's Katana attack still landed, and the Katana passed to Judy after results (R8). A line saying "a holder killed by revenge still makes that night's Katana attack" would remove the guesswork.
3) R8 says the living Yakuza are "told who holds it now". It's unclear whether a Yakuza who died that night still gets the night summary. I sent Dave no Night 3 summary, but Heidi and Judy got one.
4) Diviner neighbor groups when nearby seats are dead, and the Diviner skipping themself. The Night 1 group for Grace skipped Heidi and went on to Ivan. All three results checked out: Serial Killer, Juror and Cardinal were the in-game decoys, and Cartographer, Wiretap and Cartographer were the out-of-game ones.
- Get a "who visited whom" table generated for each night, to check the Tracker results and trap triggers before sending them.

answers.bugs_or_oddities:
- Inconsistent result wording. Night 2: "Your Katana attack on Frank tonight succeeded." Night 3: "Your Katana attack on Niaj succeeds tonight. You did not use your puppet token: 1 puppet token left." That's a tense change plus an unrequested token note that appeared only once. Erin's results also switched from "Your attack on Frank tonight succeeded" to "You attacked Niaj tonight. Your attack succeeds." These should come from one template.
- Bob's claims were cut to 40 words with a program note. The rules (R22) never mention a word limit on ledger claims, so players can't plan for it, and the truncation hid Bob's key vote statements.

  - Both pairs for Frank, the Seer: Erin/Carol and Mallory/Alice.

  - The double-cause death messages for Frank and Niaj.

answers.suggestions:

- Give the Jester's revenge (and the Executioner's) an explicit resolution order, matching the Cardinal's wording.
- Document the claim-ledger word limit in R22.
- Give the moderator structured state:
  - the current circle, with dead players marked
  - a per-player, per-Day vote matrix, for Juror, Auditor, Scrutineer and Informant results

  - trait holders

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Before accepting or making a role claim, check the setup's exclusion list (here Vanilla Villager and Grunt are never in the game). A claim of an impossible role is a near-certain lie or a sign of a Jester, and it cost me credibility on Day 2 that a plain 'I have no night action, name no role' would not have.

Check each claimed role against the rules' faction lists. Heidi's Diviner claim was a Yakuza-only role; the town flagged it on Day 5, which is a clean mechanical test that doesn't rely on who pushed hardest.

Pair the Katana with a Serial Killer or other attack on the same night to kill info roles (Seer, Tracker, Coroner). The Yakuza killed Frank, Niaj and Carol this way, which removed nearly all the town's investigative results before they could be cross-checked.

When a Jester is possible, keep the Guilty total to a bare majority and vote Innocent with power roles, since a hanged Jester's revenge kills a random Guilty voter. On Day 3 the 8-4 vote let the revenge kill Dave, a Village player, and it was avoidable.

A Jester wins fastest by self-nominating once the town is already split and has a pattern to point at. The pattern alone (a thin push plus a fake claim plus 'hang me') got eight Guilty votes, so a Jester should give a plausible real role rather than an impossible one.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the rules before calling a contradiction: actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block or swap explains a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: The town and I used the setup exclusions (Vanilla Villager not in game) to expose my fake claim, and Ivan's profile results were checked against the faction lists.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wants it (self-nominations, reckless lies). If you hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority with power roles Innocent, because revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
tips_feedback.why: The town hanged me on an 8-4 vote and ignored the caution about revenge, so Dave died to the Jester's revenge; the tip was clearly relevant and not followed.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows someone is Yakuza, look next at whoever defended them or argued for delay. A player merely caught lying may be a Jester.
tips_feedback.why: The town's suspicion of my pushes and fake claim pointed toward me as a possible Jester, which led to the hang I wanted, though it was the town's pattern reading rather than a mechanical proof.

tips_feedback.why: Frank posted his Night 1 Seer pair on Day 2. That single result drove the Village's case against Erin, and it led to her hanging on Day 4.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's future results narrow your team (Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller) before someone whose result is already posted.
tips_feedback.why: Our Katana targeted Frank, then Niaj, Carol and Ivan. Ivan's accurate profiles on Mallory and Erin were narrowing the Yakuza, so removing him made sense. The tip was reasonable, though it did not save me from Olivia's Vigilante shot.

lessons.tip: Before accepting or making a role claim, check the setup's exclusion list (here Vanilla Villager and Grunt are never in the game). A claim of an impossible role is a near-certain lie or a sign of a Jester, and it cost me credibility on Day 2 that a plain 'I have no night action, name no role' would not have.

Check each claimed role against the rules' faction lists. Heidi's Diviner claim was a Yakuza-only role; the town flagged it on Day 5, which is a clean mechanical test that doesn't rely on who pushed hardest.

Pair the Katana with a Serial Killer or other attack on the same night to kill info roles (Seer, Tracker, Coroner). The Yakuza killed Frank, Niaj and Carol this way, which removed nearly all the town's investigative results before they could be cross-checked.

When a Jester is possible, keep the Guilty total to a bare majority and vote Innocent with power roles, since a hanged Jester's revenge kills a random Guilty voter. On Day 3 the 8-4 vote let the revenge kill Dave, a Village player, and it was avoidable.

A Jester wins fastest by self-nominating once the town is already split and has a pattern to point at. The pattern alone (a thin push plus a fake claim plus 'hang me') got eight Guilty votes, so a Jester should give a plausible real role rather than an impossible one.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the rules before calling a contradiction: actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block or swap explains a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: The town and I used the setup exclusions (Vanilla Villager not in game) to expose my fake claim, and Ivan's profile results were checked against the faction lists.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wants it (self-nominations, reckless lies). If you hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority with power roles Innocent, because revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
tips_feedback.why: The town hanged me on an 8-4 vote and ignored the caution about revenge, so Dave died to the Jester's revenge; the tip was clearly relevant and not followed.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows someone is Yakuza, look next at whoever defended them or argued for delay. A player merely caught lying may be a Jester.
tips_feedback.why: The town's suspicion of my pushes and fake claim pointed toward me as a possible Jester, which led to the hang I wanted, though it was the town's pattern reading rather than a mechanical proof.

lessons.applies_to: Tracker, Lookout, Seer and other info roles
lessons.tip: Post each night result publicly on the next Day, as soon as it comes in. My Night 3 result (Erin visited Niaj, the night of the Serial Killer attack on me) was never shared, and it died with me in my will. A held-back result is worth nothing if you die before the Day.

When a kill is made by a Serial Killer or Katana, check which player visited the victim that night. A tracked or watched visit to a victim is stronger evidence than any claim, so match visits against deaths before trusting anyone's pair or profile.

A player who pushes a trial on a thin read, claims an impossible role and then says 'hang me' may be a Jester who wants the hang. Ask the accused for a real role before voting Guilty, and remember that a hanged Jester wins immediately, so a mass Guilty vote on a suspected Jester gives them the game.

Check the role list for impossible claims. The Diviner is Yakuza-only in these rules, so a Diviner claim from a Good player is a lie or a Yakuza claim. Catch such claims early, because a Yakuza who defends one may be hiding in the open.
Before a hang, ask what the reveal settles. A Coroner examining a dead Seer proves the role but not what the Seer's pair saw, so do not treat a confirmed role as a confirmed result when voting.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote in your first speech, with night, target and exact result.
tips_feedback.why: I posted my Night 2 Tracker result on Day 3 and the Serial Killer and Katana killed me that night. Publishing results made my role an obvious target, and the Village still gained little because the Yakuza had already read the posts.

tips_feedback.why: Mallory did want the hang, and I flagged the Jester pattern, but the Village still voted 8 Guilty. The hang handed the Jester the win, so the tip identified the problem without changing the outcome.

tips_feedback.why: Most Village players voted Guilty, and the Jester's revenge then killed Dave, a Village player, the night after the hang. The advice was not followed, and the cost was a Village death.

tips_feedback.tip: Examine bodies that settle a live question, not an undisputed Katana victim.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's Coroner exam of Frank confirmed he was a real Seer, which made his Night 1 pair (Erin vs Carol) credible. That supported the later Erin hang, and Erin was indeed the Serial Killer, so the exam was useful.

lessons.tip: Fire your first shot on the first credible Yakuza lead (a PM cluster with a claimant, a defended Yakuza-only claim, an unexplained visit), not after several Days of waiting. I held all three tokens through Nights 1-4 while the Katana killed Carol and Ivan, and only shot on Night 5, when Judy was the last Yakuza. An earlier shot might have removed the Katana holder before two more deaths.

Check which side a claimed role belongs to in the rules before trusting it. Heidi's Diviner claim was a Yakuza-only role, and the Village used that to hang her. Any Good player claiming a Yakuza-only or Neutral-only role is a strong lead.

Ask a suspected Jester directly whether they are one, and watch how they answer. Mallory's fake Vanilla claim, the push on Frank's trial and the 'hang me' line matched a Jester, and the hang was correct, though it gave the Jester a win. Before voting, check whether a Jester win is acceptable for your side, and keep Guilty votes to a bare majority when power roles are alive.

Make Day 2 productive. Almost every Village player posted the same 'no nomination until more results' line for two Days, which gave the Yakuza time and let one Jester drive the only trial. Agree early on a concrete checking order (who posts a result, who gets tested first) so the town is not stalled for a whole Day.
Repeating 'no nomination from me, still waiting' costs budget and adds no information. Spend budget on specific questions and checkable results, which are what actually moved the votes this game.

tips_feedback.why: I ignored it and waited until Night 5 with three tokens. The shot did kill the last Yakuza, but the Katana had already killed Carol and Ivan while I waited.

tips_feedback.why: Judy defended Heidi's Yakuza-only Diviner claim and had PMs with her on Days 4-5, which pointed to the remaining Yakuza pair.

tips_feedback.why: The Serial Killer attacks on Frank and Niaj showed a Neutral killer was alive. Erin fit that profile, and hanging her was correct.

summary: The Village won, and Mallory, the Jester, also won by getting hanged. Three things decided the game. First, Heidi (Yakuza) publicly called herself a Diviner on Day 2, which is a Yakuza-only role. The town didn't notice until Ivan pointed it out on Day 5. Once he did, she was hanged at once, and her open defender Judy became Olivia's Vigilante target that night. Second, the town combined several results well to hang Erin, the Serial Killer, on Day 4. Frank's Night 1 Seer pair (Erin/Carol different) was confirmed when Carol's Coroner exam showed Frank was a real Seer. Ivan's profile of Erin (Juror/SK/Wiretap) plus Bob's Juror claim left Erin as non-Good. Third, the town hanged the Jester on Day 3 with 8 Guilty votes, more than it needed. The Jester's revenge, which hits a random Guilty voter, happened to kill Dave, the Yakuza Katana holder, who still had his unused puppet token. With 8 Guilty voters it could easily have killed Ivan or Niaj instead. The Yakuza made other mistakes too. They skipped the Night 1 kill. Twice the Katana and the Serial Killer attacked the same obvious investigator (Frank on Night 2, Niaj on Night 3), which wasted two kills. Heidi and Judy sent each other private messages during the Day, and the town treated that link as a lead. Judy also voted Innocent in trials, which helped mark her. Olivia sat on all 3 Vigilante shots until Night 5, then used one Basic shot on Judy, the last Yakuza, which ended the game.

lessons.tip: Never name your real role if it's Yakuza-only, even in passing (for example 'as Diviner I get no visit notices'). Choose a Village cover role on Night 1 that fits your real visits, and if you must say something about yourself, describe it in terms that cover role allows.
lessons.evidence: Heidi said 'I get no visit notices as Diviner' on Day 2. On Day 5 Ivan pointed out that Diviner is Yakuza-only, and she was nominated and hanged 5-2 within one round.

lessons.tip: Check every role claim against the rules as soon as it's made: is it a Yakuza-only role, or a role this setup never uses (Vanilla Villager)? Either one breaks the claim at once and should be called out that Day, not three Days later.
lessons.evidence: Ivan caught Mallory's Vanilla claim the morning after she made it, but nobody noticed Heidi's Diviner slip from Day 2 to Day 5. During that time two more Villagers died to the Katana (Niaj, Carol).

lessons.tip: If someone self-nominates after a role claim that can't exist, treat them as a likely Jester. Hanging them is fine (Jesters never block your win), but keep the Guilty count near a bare majority and keep your proven information roles on Innocent, because revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
lessons.evidence: Mallory nominated herself after an impossible Vanilla claim, and Ivan's profile listed Jester. The trial went 8 Guilty to 4 Innocent, and Ivan and Niaj both voted Guilty. The revenge hit Dave (Yakuza) only by luck.

lessons.tip: Combine results by elimination. A three-role profile becomes an alignment read once claims you trust rule out the Good option, and a Coroner exam that confirms a dead investigator's role makes that investigator's posted results trustworthy.
lessons.evidence: Erin's profile was Juror/SK/Wiretap and Bob had claimed Juror, so Erin was non-Good. Carol's exam showed Frank was a real Seer, which backed his Erin/Carol pair. Together they got the Serial Killer hanged 6-3. Judy's profile (Cardinal/Cartographer/Informant) next to Grace's Cardinal claim set up Olivia's later shot on Judy.

lessons.tip: Once a Neutral killer has shown up, or is likely, don't spend the Katana on the single most obvious investigator, because the killer will probably hit them too. Aim at the second-biggest threat, and use your Night 1 kill and one-shot tokens (puppet) instead of saving them.
lessons.evidence: The Katana and the Serial Killer both attacked Frank on Night 2 and Niaj on Night 3, so the Yakuza got no extra kills. They also skipped the Night 1 attack, and Dave died still holding his puppet token.

lessons.tip: Do all planning in night chat and send no Day private messages to teammates. Once a teammate is doomed, don't defend them or vote Innocent unless your votes can actually save them, because a Juror or the town's lists of stated votes will tie you to them.
lessons.evidence: Judy and Heidi messaged each other privately on Days 4 and 5, and Ivan, Olivia, Grace and Bob all asked what the messages were about. Judy publicly defended Heidi and voted Innocent in a 5-2 hang, and Olivia shot her that night because of it.

lessons.tip: Fire a Basic shot as soon as there's a reasonable lead, such as an impossible role claim or a defender of one. Don't wait for proof, because unused shots are lost if you die.
lessons.evidence: Olivia held all 3 tokens from Night 1 to Night 4 even though Heidi had been publicly claiming Diviner since Day 2. Her first shot, a Basic on Judy on Night 5, won the game. An earlier shot on Heidi might have saved Carol or Niaj.

lessons.tip: Don't announce that you'll use a token tonight or whom you plan to test. Do put tonight's planned target in your will, so the town can work out the result if you die.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 Frank announced he would use his last token that night and test Mallory's 'pattern'. Both the Katana and the Serial Killer killed him that night. His will left out his Mallory/Alice check, so the town only learned the pair from Niaj's tracking, and never learned the result.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree cover claims on Night 1 that fit your token count and real visits. Using Yakuza-only role names, leaking night-chat knowledge or switching claims once cornered tends to hang you.
tips_feedback.why: The game proved this tip right. Heidi ignored it by naming Diviner and was hanged on Day 5 the moment someone noticed.

tips_feedback.tip: Plan in night chat, not daytime PMs: everyone sees who messaged whom, and a visible PM cluster often becomes the town's lead.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi and Judy ignored it, and four Villagers used their visible private-message link as the case against Judy, which ended with Olivia shooting her.

tips_feedback.tip: Defend a doomed teammate only if night-chat vote math says your votes can save them; otherwise vote Guilty with the town and say so, because totals get compared with stated votes.
tips_feedback.why: Judy defended Heidi and voted Innocent in a hopeless 5-2 trial, which marked her as the Vigilante's target and lost the game for the Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wants it (self-nominations, reckless lies). If you hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority with power roles Innocent, because revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
tips_feedback.why: Several players (Niaj, Olivia, Alice, Bob, Grace) spotted the Jester signs, and Bob, Grace and Olivia voted Innocent. But 8 Guilty votes, including Ivan's, still put power roles at risk, and the revenge hit the Yakuza only by luck.

tips_feedback.tip: Examine bodies that settle a live question (a hanged suspect, one side of a duplicate claim), not an undisputed Katana victim. Post night, target and exact role the next Day, and avoid announcing tomorrow's exam.
tips_feedback.why: Carol examined Frank to check his disputed Seer pair. The confirmation was the key to hanging Erin, the Serial Killer.

tips_feedback.tip: Set a concrete trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a good lead rather than waiting for proof; dying with unused shots is the usual failure.
tips_feedback.why: When Olivia finally fired a Basic shot on a good lead (Judy), it won the game. Her delay until Night 5 shows the cost of waiting.

tips_feedback.tip: Dead players spend nothing: use one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, ritual guess, shots) on the first night they can change a vote or remove a threat, because holders who wait usually die with them.
tips_feedback.why: Dave saved his puppet token 'for a later Day' and died to the Jester's revenge without ever using it.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or that you will act, publicly or by PM: it tells blockers and the Katana where to go, and a Wiretap may read every PM.
tips_feedback.why: Frank kept announcing that he would use his Seer token on Night 2, and he was killed by both the Katana and the Serial Killer that night before he could post the result.

issues.description: Heidi (Yakuza Diviner) publicly named her real role on Day 2 ('I get no visit notices as Diviner'), even though Diviner is listed only under Yakuza roles. Dave privately warned her, but she kept the claim. On Day 5 the Village noticed it was a Yakuza-only role and hanged her for it. She seems not to have realized her role name exposes her faction.

Ivan and Bob (Day 4) argued that because Bob claims Juror, Erin's profile (Juror/Serial Killer/Wiretap) can't be Juror. The setup says roles may repeat except unique ones (Smuggler, Vulture), so Bob's claim doesn't rule out Erin being a Juror.

Mallory's Day 3 claim said 'Day 2: No on Frank's nomination (I nominated him)'. The nominator votes Yes by default, and the log shows Mallory voted Yes. The claim contradicts itself and is false (possibly a Jester bluff, but it reads like confusion about the nominator's default vote).
The claim ledger cuts claims at 40 words (Bob's was cut twice). Grace and Frank said in the debrief that this hid part of Bob's vote history, which made checking votes harder.

Players hit output-format friction: Ivan's StructuredOutput failed to parse when he wrote unquoted nulls inside a raw JSON string; Dave had to fill every required field with placeholders (claim, last will); Heidi found that names in quotes were rejected in the Katana vote fields. The schema should accept empty or optional fields and normalize name strings.
